---
title: Submitting a tool
description: How to tell us about a redaction tool we are missing, what an editor does with it, and why a submission is never a live page.
---

Use [the submission form](/submit). You will need an account — that is the only anti-spam
measure here, and it is what keeps the queue readable.

Anyone can submit. You do not have to work for the vendor, and submitting does not claim
the listing.

## What happens next

**A submission is a queue item, never a live page.** Nothing you write is published on
submission, and there is no delay after which it goes live by itself.

**An editor checks the tool, writes the listing in our own words, and records the pricing
from the vendor's published page.** Your description is not published verbatim. This is not
a slight on your writing — a catalog where each entry is written by a different interested
party is not a comparison, and the several-hundred-word minimum for a listing exists
precisely so that every page was written by someone comparing it against the others.

**Until a listing has been reviewed, its outbound links carry `rel="nofollow"`.**
Submitting is not a way to buy a link.

**If you work for the vendor, claim the listing afterwards.** That is a separate step —
see [claiming a listing](/docs/vendors/claiming-a-listing) — and it is what lets you
propose corrections later.

## What makes a submission easy to act on

A tool becomes a page only once it clears [the listing
bar](/docs/methodology#what-a-listing-has-to-clear). You can save an editor a round of
research by including:

- The **product URL**, not a marketing landing page.
- The **pricing page**, if there is a public one. If there is not, say so — that is a fact
  about the product and we record it as one, rather than leaving the tool out.
- **What it redacts** (PDF, image, video, audio, text), **how it is deployed** (online,
  desktop, self-hosted, API, extension) and **how it decides what to cover** (manual,
  rule-based, AI, hybrid). Those three are required before anything can be listed.
- Anything that distinguishes it. "It is the only one that does X" is genuinely useful, and
  it is checkable.

## Corrections

The same form takes corrections to existing listings. If a price here is wrong, this is the
fastest way to tell us, whoever you are.
